edges.description: Reduced maternal-to-fetal calcium flux lowers fetal circulating calcium.

The intrauterine calcium deficit is measurable postnatally as low serum calcium in about two thirds of neonates. In the published series the neonates who were normocalcaemic at birth were those without vitamin D deficiency, so maternal and neonatal vitamin D status, rather than the degree of parathyroid compensation, is what the evidence links to whether hypocalcaemia is present at presentation.
Low circulating calcium drives compensatory parathyroid hormone secretion in the fetus.
Sustained PTH mobilises calcium from the only remaining reservoir, the fetal skeleton.
The endocrine response is itself the presenting clinical and biochemical finding.

PTH lowers renal tubular phosphate reabsorption, so sustained secondary hyperparathyroidism can lower serum phosphate. The intermediate step has not been measured in this disease, and only a minority of reported neonates were hypophosphataemic, so the edge records the expected route rather than a demonstrated one.
Mineral withdrawn from bone, together with inadequate mineral delivery, leaves the skeleton undermineralised.

High bone turnover releases alkaline phosphatase into the circulation. The marker reports turnover as a whole, so it keeps rising after birth as remineralisation begins and is the last value to normalise.
Undermineralised, fractured, short and deformed ribs give a narrow, bell-shaped thorax that cannot support adequate ventilation.

nodes.description: TRPV6 provides the apical calcium entry step of transcellular calcium movement across the syncytiotrophoblast, the transporting epithelium of the human placenta. Because fetal blood calcium is held above the maternal concentration, this transfer is uphill and depends on an active transcellular route rather than paracellular leak, so losing the entry channel cannot be compensated by diffusion. Transcript levels rise sharply in late gestation as fetal mineral demand peaks, which is why the deficit manifests in the third trimester.

nodes.description: After birth the infant no longer depends on the placenta for calcium. This is the mechanism the word "transient" in the disease name refers to. It is an explanation reconstructed from the consistent clinical course rather than a directly measured one, and recovery is not invariably complete.

nodes.description: Biallelic TRPV6 variants abolish or severely reduce calcium flux through the channel. The reported mechanisms are heterogeneous: frameshift and nonsense alleles truncate the protein, splice-altering alleles reduce functional transcript, and missense alleles act by mislocalisation - some failing to traffic to the plasma membrane, others retained in the endoplasmic reticulum or not delivered to intracellular vesicles - or by destabilising the tetramer. A few missense alleles retain near-normal unitary conductance and cause disease through reduced surface abundance rather than altered gating.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations That Affect the Surface Expression of TRPV6 Are Associated with the Upregulation of Serine Proteases in the Placenta of an Infant.
evidence.snippet: One mutation results in an in frame stop codon (R510stop) that leads to a truncated, nonfunctional TRPV6 channel, and the second in a point mutation (G660R) that, surprisingly, does not affect the Ca2+ permeability of TRPV6.

nodes.description: A recurrent missense allele found both in this disease and in patients with chronic pancreatitis. It retains channel activity but is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and is not delivered to intracellular vesicles, which is the proposed basis of its pathogenicity.

evidence.reference_title: TRPV6 Gene Mutation in a Dizygous Twin With Transient Neonatal Hyperparathyroidism.
evidence.snippet: Our analysis of TRPV6 gene clarified that the patient had compound heterozygote mutations, which were reported previously (p.Ile223Thr and p.Gly428Arg).

evidence.reference_title: The intracellular localization and the ionic permeation of TRPV6 triggers chronic pancreatitis, skeletal dysplasia and is connected to mucolipidosis type II.
evidence.snippet: We show that a TRPV6 mutation, I223T, frequently found in patients with pancreatitis/skeletal dysplasia sticks to the ER but shows not reduced channel activity.

nodes.description: A monoallelic, paternally inherited missense variant adjacent to the TRP box, the single reported dominant-negative allele. The protein reaches the plasma membrane normally, but coimmunoprecipitation, calcium imaging and patch-clamp show it impairs the channel by forming a heteromer with the wild-type subunit. This is a single reported case and does not establish a dominant mode of inheritance for the disease: the father's own neonatal history was not available, so penetrance of the variant in him is unknown, and every other published case is biallelic.

evidence.reference_title: Transient neonatal hyperparathyroidism caused by a monoallelic TRPV6 dominant negative variant.
evidence.snippet: However, coimmunoprecipitation, intracellular calcium imaging, and patch-clamp studies suggested that the p.Val625Glu variant exerts a dominant-negative effect by interacting with the wild-type subunit to form a heteromeric complex, thereby impairing channel function.

evidence.reference_title: Transient neonatal hyperparathyroidism caused by a monoallelic TRPV6 dominant negative variant.
evidence.snippet: Whole exome sequencing identified a novel paternally inherited heterozygous missense variant in the TRPV6 gene resulting in a valine-to-glutamic acid substitution at codon 625 (p.Val625Glu).
